questions.question: Has the vendor stated in writing the intended purpose, intended users and clinical setting of the AI-CDSS?
questions.guidance: Request a written statement of intended use before adoption, and do not use the system outside that purpose.
questions.source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration et al. (2024)

questions.question: Has the vendor described the data used to train and test the system, including the population and setting it came from?
questions.guidance: Ask the vendor for a description of its training and testing data, and check whether patients like yours were included.
questions.source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration et al. (2024)

questions.question: Has the vendor provided evidence of the system's performance and explained how it was validated?
questions.guidance: Request the vendor's performance figures and validation reports, and do not rely on marketing claims alone.

questions.question: Does the vendor's evidence show whether the system works equally well for different patient groups?
questions.guidance: Ask for the study results, and check that fairness across patient groups was assessed.

questions.question: Has the vendor disclosed the system's known limitations and the situations in which it should not be used?
questions.guidance: Ask for a summary of limitations and contraindications, and share it with clinical users.

questions.question: Has the system been tested on patients or data from a setting similar to your institution?
questions.guidance: Arrange a local evaluation or pilot before full adoption, because performance may not carry over from other settings.
questions.source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration et al. (2024)

questions.question: Has the institution's ethics committee reviewed the AI-CDSS before it is deployed?
questions.guidance: Refer the system to the ethics committee for review before go-live, and record its decision.

questions.question: Can clinicians see the basis for each recommendation, and not only the output?
questions.guidance: Ask the vendor how recommendations can be reviewed; if they cannot, limit use to tasks where clinicians can check the result independently.

questions.question: Do clinicians see a confidence or certainty level with each recommendation?
questions.guidance: Ask the vendor whether confidence information can be displayed, and train clinicians to treat low-confidence outputs with caution.

questions.question: Have the clinicians who will use the system been trained on how it works and on its limits?
questions.guidance: Provide training before go-live, covering what the system does, its limits and when not to rely on it.

questions.question: Is it clear that clinicians remain responsible for the final decision and can override the system?
questions.guidance: State in local policy that the clinician makes the final decision and may disagree with the system.

questions.question: Do patients receive plain-language information about the AI-CDSS used in their care?
questions.guidance: Prepare plain-language information on what the system does and how its results are used, and include it in patient information and consent processes.

questions.question: Has the institution agreed what patients will be told about how the AI contributed to a decision about them, and who will tell them?
questions.guidance: Agree a standard explanation for patients and assign responsibility for giving it, usually the treating clinician.

questions.question: Has a data protection impact assessment been carried out before the system processes patient data?
questions.guidance: Complete a data protection impact assessment with the data protection officer before go-live.

questions.question: Does the institution keep an up-to-date inventory of all AI tools in clinical use?
questions.guidance: Create a register of AI tools, recording each tool's purpose, vendor, owner and date of adoption.
questions.source: National Institute of Standards and Technology (2023)

questions.question: Does the institution record which version of the system is in use and when it changes?
questions.guidance: Record the version number at adoption and after every update, so that recommendations can be traced to a version.

questions.question: Are the system's recommendations, and the decisions made with them, logged so they can be reviewed later?
questions.guidance: Agree with the vendor how logs are kept and for how long, and make sure they can be retrieved if a problem occurs.

questions.question: Does the vendor notify the institution before updating or changing the system?
questions.guidance: Include a requirement in the contract for advance notice of updates, with a description of what has changed.
questions.source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration et al. (2024)

questions.question: Does the institution monitor the system's performance after it goes live?
questions.guidance: Assign someone to review performance at set intervals, because performance can fall when patients, data or practice change.

questions.question: Is there a process for staff to report errors or concerns about the system to the institution and the vendor?
questions.guidance: Create a reporting route for AI-related incidents, and agree with the vendor how reported problems will be handled.
